title: How do you write a CV that gets you a consulting interview?
description: What consulting recruiters look for on a CV, how to write achievement-led bullet points with numbers, and common mistakes to avoid.
hook: Your CV has one job: get you into the interview room. Consulting recruiters often read hundreds of CVs, quickly. The good news is that what they look for is consistent, and a few changes can make a big difference.
body:
What recruiters look for

  • Academic strength: grades, rankings, scholarships, test scores where relevant.
  • Achievement: results you delivered, not just responsibilities you had.
  • Leadership: times you led people, started something or took ownership.
  • Something distinctive: a sport at a high level, a business you started, a cause you built.

Write bullet points like results

Start each bullet with an action verb, say what you did, and finish with the result, with a number if you can.

  • Weak: "Responsible for the society's marketing."
  • Strong: "Redesigned the society's social media plan, growing event attendance from 40 to 150 in one term."

Keep it clean

  • One page for students and early-career candidates.
  • A simple, consistent layout. No photos, graphics or colours unless that is the local norm.
  • Most recent first. Education at the top for students.
  • Check every number, date and spelling. Mistakes suggest a lack of attention to detail, which consultants care about.

Cover letters

Keep them short and specific: why consulting, why this firm (mention people you spoke to or work that interests you), and two or three pieces of evidence that you would be good at it.

Sources

  • TARGETjobs: Applying to McKinsey (CVs and cover letters)

Checked November 2026.
